createServer: Creates an `HTTPServer`. If `onrequest` is given, it's added as a `'request'` listener.
request: Creates an `HTTPClientRequest` to `url` (a `URL` or a URL string). If `onresponse` is given, it's added as a one-time `'response'` listener. Does not send the request until it's ended.
get: Like `request()`, but ends the request immediately, since GET requests have no body.
constants: The `method` map of supported HTTP method names and the `status` map of status codes to their reason phrases.
HTTPMethod: A key of `constants.method`, i.e. one of the supported HTTP method names.
HTTPStatusCode: A key of `constants.status`, i.e. a supported HTTP status code.
HTTPStatusMessage: The reason phrase for a given `HTTPStatusCode`, as found in `constants.status`.
HTTPError: An error thrown by `bare-http1` for protocol-level failures, such as an unimplemented method, a lost connection, a suspended agent, or an invalid header. Carries a `code` identifying the specific failure.
METHODS: The list of all supported HTTP method names.
STATUS_CODES: An alias for `constants.status`, mapping status codes to their reason phrases.
HTTPIncomingMessageEvents: The events an `HTTPIncomingMessage` emits in addition to the underlying readable stream's events: `timeout`, when the socket times out.
HTTPIncomingMessageOptions: Options for constructing an `HTTPIncomingMessage` directly: initial `headers`, `method`, `url` (server-side), and `statusCode`/`statusMessage` (client-side).
HTTPIncomingMessage: A readable stream representing an incoming HTTP request (on the server) or response (on the client). Carries the parsed `headers`, `method`/`url` or `statusCode`/`statusMessage`, and the underlying `socket`.
HTTPIncomingMessage.getHeader: Returns the value of header `name` (case-insensitive), or `undefined` if not set.
HTTPIncomingMessage.getHeaders: Returns a shallow copy of all headers.
HTTPIncomingMessage.headers: The parsed headers, keyed by lowercase name.
HTTPIncomingMessage.httpVersion: The HTTP version of the message. Always `'1.1'`.
HTTPIncomingMessage.method: The request method. Only meaningful on the server side.
HTTPIncomingMessage.setTimeout: Sets the underlying socket's timeout to `ms` and, if given, adds `ontimeout` as a one-time `'timeout'` listener.
HTTPIncomingMessage.socket: The underlying `TCPSocket` the message was read from.
HTTPIncomingMessage.statusCode: The response status code. Only meaningful on the client side.
HTTPIncomingMessage.statusMessage: The response status reason phrase. Only meaningful on the client side.
HTTPIncomingMessage.upgrade: Whether the connection was upgraded (e.g. to a WebSocket) after this message.
HTTPOutgoingMessageEvents: The events an `HTTPOutgoingMessage` emits in addition to the underlying writable stream's events: `timeout`, when the socket times out.
HTTPOutgoingMessage: A writable stream representing an outgoing HTTP request (on the client) or response (on the server). Base class of `HTTPClientRequest` and `HTTPServerResponse`.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.flushHeaders: Sends the headers immediately, if they haven't already been sent, instead of waiting for the first write.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.getHeader: Returns the value of header `name` (case-insensitive), or `undefined` if not set.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.getHeaders: Returns a shallow copy of all headers set so far.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.headers: The headers set so far, keyed by lowercase name. Assigning validates each header name and value.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.headersSent: Whether the headers have already been sent.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.setTimeout: Sets the underlying socket's timeout to `ms` and, if given, adds `ontimeout` as a one-time `'timeout'` listener.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.socket: The underlying `TCPSocket` the message is written to.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.upgrade: Whether the connection was upgraded (e.g. to a WebSocket) after this message.
HTTPAgentOptions: Options for `HTTPAgent`. `keepAlive` keeps sockets open for reuse after a request completes, either `true` (using `keepAliveMsecs`) or a number of milliseconds. `keepAliveMsecs` is the keep-alive duration when `keepAlive` is `true`, defaulting to `1000`.
globalAgent: The default `HTTPAgent` used by `request()` and `get()` when no `agent` option is given.
HTTPAgent: Manages a pool of `TCPSocket` connections shared across requests to the same host and port, reusing idle keep-alive sockets instead of opening a new connection per request.
HTTPAgent.addRequest: Assigns a socket to `req`, reusing an idle keep-alive socket for the same host and port if one is available, or creating a new one otherwise.
HTTPAgent.createConnection: Creates a new `TCPSocket` connection for a request. Throws if the agent is suspended.
HTTPAgent.destroy: Destroys all sockets currently held by the agent, both in-use and free.
HTTPAgent.freeSockets: An iterator over the agent's idle, keep-alive sockets awaiting reuse.
HTTPAgent.getName: Returns the pool key used to group sockets by destination, derived from `opts.host` and `opts.port`.
HTTPAgent.global: The agent's own default instance, used as `bare-http1`'s `globalAgent`.
HTTPAgent.keepSocketAlive: Marks `socket` to be kept alive and unreferenced instead of closed once a request completes. Returns whether the socket was kept alive.
HTTPAgent.resume: Resumes an agent suspended with `suspend()`, allowing it to create connections again.
HTTPAgent.resumed: A promise that resolves once a suspended agent is resumed, or `null` if the agent isn't suspended.
HTTPAgent.reuseSocket: Marks `socket` as back in active use, referencing it so it keeps the event loop alive.
HTTPAgent.sockets: An iterator over all sockets currently held by the agent, both in-use and free.
HTTPAgent.suspend: Suspends the agent, destroying all its sockets and preventing new connections until `resume()` is called.
HTTPAgent.suspended: Whether the agent is currently suspended.
HTTPServerEvents: The events an `HTTPServer` emits in addition to the underlying TCP server's events: `request`, for each incoming request; `timeout`, when a connection's socket times out; `upgrade`, when a connection is upgraded (e.g. to a WebSocket).
HTTPServer: An HTTP/1.1 server, extending `TCPServer`. Emits `'request'` with an `HTTPIncomingMessage` and `HTTPServerResponse` for each request received.
HTTPServer.setTimeout: Sets the idle-socket timeout to `ms` (default `0`, meaning no timeout) and, if given, adds `ontimeout` as a `'timeout'` listener.
HTTPServer.timeout: The idle-socket timeout in milliseconds, or `undefined` if none is set.
HTTPServerResponse: An outgoing HTTP response, extending `HTTPOutgoingMessage`. Defaults to status `200` and chunked transfer encoding unless a `Content-Length` header is set.
HTTPServerResponse.statusCode: The response status code to send. Defaults to `200`.
HTTPServerResponse.statusMessage: The response status reason phrase to send. Defaults to the standard phrase for `statusCode`.
HTTPServerResponse.writeHead: Sets `statusCode`, and optionally `statusMessage` and additional `headers`, in one call.
HTTPServerConnectionOptions: Options for `HTTPServerConnection`, letting custom `IncomingMessage` and `ServerResponse` subclasses be used for requests handled on the connection.
HTTPServerConnection: The per-socket state machine that parses incoming request data into `HTTPIncomingMessage`/`HTTPServerResponse` pairs for an `HTTPServer`.
HTTPServerConnection.for: Returns the `HTTPServerConnection` associated with `socket`, or `null` if none exists.
HTTPServerConnection.idle: Whether the connection currently has no in-flight request.
HTTPServerConnection.req: The `HTTPIncomingMessage` currently being read on this connection, or `null` if none.
HTTPServerConnection.res: The `HTTPServerResponse` currently being written on this connection, or `null` if none.
HTTPClientRequestEvents: The events an `HTTPClientRequest` emits in addition to the underlying writable stream's events: `response`, with the `HTTPIncomingMessage` reply; `upgrade`, when the connection is upgraded (e.g. to a WebSocket).
HTTPClientRequestOptions: Options for `HTTPClientRequest`: the `agent` to use (or `false` for a fresh, unpooled one), request `headers`, `method` (default `'GET'`), and `path` (default `'/'`).
HTTPClientRequest: An outgoing HTTP request, extending `HTTPOutgoingMessage`. Uses chunked transfer encoding unless a `Content-Length` header is set or the method is `GET`/`HEAD`.
HTTPClientRequest.headers: The headers to send with the request, keyed by lowercase name, including an auto-generated `host` header.
HTTPClientConnectionOptions: Options for `HTTPClientConnection`, letting a custom `IncomingMessage` subclass be used for the response.
HTTPClientConnection: The per-socket state machine that parses response data for an `HTTPClientRequest`, and drives its `'response'` event.
HTTPClientConnection.for: Returns the `HTTPClientConnection` associated with `socket`, or `null` if none exists.
HTTPClientConnection.from: Returns the existing `HTTPClientConnection` for `socket`, creating one with `opts` if none exists yet.
HTTPClientConnection.idle: Whether the connection currently has no in-flight request.
HTTPClientConnection.req: The `HTTPClientRequest` currently in flight on this connection, or `null` if none.
HTTPClientConnection.res: The `HTTPIncomingMessage` currently being read on this connection, or `null` if none.
